case_role: Largest segmentation-induced EF error; most confident misclassification
observed_pattern: Segmentation-associated EF propagation error with confidently incorrect classification
interpretation: GT-geometry EF was 47.49%, whereas predicted-geometry EF was 29.44%, corresponding to an 18.06 pp segmentation-induced EF difference. The final EF-band prediction was incorrect despite a high uncalibrated classifier confidence score of 0.888.

Reference EF was 19.00%, whereas EF derived from GT-mask geometry was 67.67% and predicted-geometry EF was 61.79%. Therefore, much of the 42.79 pp end-to-end disagreement was already present between the reference EF and the 2D GT-mask-derived geometry rather than being introduced by segmentation alone.

Reference EF was exactly 50.00%, while predicted-geometry EF was 48.25%. Although the end-to-end EF disagreement was only 1.75 pp, it crossed the predefined 50% boundary and changed the EF-band assignment from Higher_EF to Intermediate_EF.

observed_pattern: Strong segmentation and small downstream disagreement
interpretation: Stored ED and ES Dice were 0.967 and 0.961, respectively. Segmentation-induced EF error was 1.48 pp and end-to-end EF error was 1.65 pp. The final Lower_EF classification was correct.
